title: queryChanges positions reflect state newer than newQueryState
description: MessageQueryChangesHandler uses two separate lock scopes (message.rs lines 815-867 and 872-887). new_state (newQueryState) is captured inside lock 1. Positions are computed inside lock 2. Between the two locks a concurrent write (e.g. Peer/deliver) can insert a new message, advancing the DB state counter. Lock 2 then computes positions against the newer DB snapshot, while new_state still reflects the pre-insert state. The client receives position indices that are inconsistent with the newQueryState token they were given: replaying those positions against newQueryState will be off-by-one or worse. The comment at lines 869-871 claims positions come from 'the same snapshot' but that invariant is not enforced — the two lock scopes are separate and the DB state can change between them.
